subject.title: EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError: session GC deletes file while agent is still running

question: Should cron/session cleanup skip active admitted work, interrupt-and-drain it, or defer this fix into the broader retention/storage lifecycle refactor?
rationale: The bug is concrete, but the safest repair crosses cron retention, active session-work admissions, and transcript storage cleanup semantics, so maintainer intent is needed before spawning another implementation path.

options.title: Guard Active Work Now
options.body: Add a focused active-admission guard to the cron/session cleanup path so active cron runs cannot have their transcripts archived mid-run, while leaving broader storage migration work separate.

options.title: Fold Into Retention Refactor
options.body: Keep this open under the larger cron retention/session storage lifecycle effort and accept the reported failure risk until that work lands.

options.title: Relax Ambiguous Pruning
options.body: Temporarily disable or broaden retention for ambiguous cron run entries until lifecycle ownership is made explicit.

recommendation.title: Guard Active Work Now
recommendation.body: Add a focused active-admission guard to the cron/session cleanup path so active cron runs cannot have their transcripts archived mid-run, while leaving broader storage migration work separate.

likelyOwner.reason: They are tied to recent session cleanup lifecycle seam work that this decision must align with.
